## HueMux v0.0.4-alpha.10 — Rooms become cards, and the color picker learns white

> **Alpha.** This release redesigns the Lights screen: rooms are collapsible
> cards with icons and color summaries, presets move to a single scrollable
> strip at the bottom, the grid column count becomes a setting, and the color
> picker gains a white-temperature strip for warm-to-cool whites.

### Rooms are collapsible cards

Each room renders as one card — archetype icon, name, light count, up to four
color-summary dots, and a chevron that collapses the whole card down to its
header. Collapsed state persists per device, survives reloads, and is ignored
by the single-room filter (navigating into a room always opens it).

### White-temperature strip in the color picker

The color picker's right edge is now a white-temperature gradient (6500 K at
the top, 2000 K at the bottom). Dragging there sets the white point directly —
the new `light_color_temp` WS message sends mirek to the bridge natively, with
no xy conversion. White-ambiance-only bulbs (color temperature but no color)
get a full-canvas temperature picker and now show a palette button at all.
Lights in CT mode tint their card from mirek rather than a stale xy.

### Light columns setting

The card grid is 2 columns on phones (1 below 360 px, where two cards don't
fit). Settings gains a **Light columns** control — 1/2/3/4, default 2 — applied
live to the Lights tab the moment it changes, per device.

### Presets strip at the bottom

Entertainment-zone scenes moved below the room cards into one horizontally
scrollable strip (no wrap, hidden scrollbar), tinted by each scene's first
swatch. Room-scoped scenes stay inside their room's card.

### Room and lamp icons

Rooms get an inline SVG icon mapped from their Hue archetype (sofa, bed,
kitchen, dining, bath, office, gym, plant, door — unknown archetypes fall back
to a house). Light cards get a lamp icon next to the name. All icons inherit
the current theme's ink color, so dark/light/simple all just work.

### What this does not do

It does not change the per-light control flow: inline brightness sliders (with
their on/dim/off quirk rules), power buttons, the tap-and-hold swipe color
picker, favorites, and the bottom navigation all behave exactly as before.
The OLED-black palette stays — this is a structural redesign, not a re-skin.
